references.text: The foundational command of the Mosaic law regarding just weights and measures, which forbids injustice in trade and requires honesty in all measuring tools.
Proverbs confirms that a false weight is an abomination to the Lord, while a correct weight brings him joy.
Emphasizes that a just balance and scales belong to the Lord, and that all the weights in the bag are his work.
Repeats that differing weights and differing measures are both an abomination to the Lord.
Condemns varying weights and states that a false weight is not good.
The prophet Amos accuses those who use dishonest scales and diminish the ephah measure to cheat the poor.
Micah condemns the unjust balances and false weights used in the house of the wicked.
Ezekiel commands that the people shall have just balances, a just ephah, and a just bath.
